newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU COURT REDUCES CMB SHIPPING FINE.
newsitem.headline: EU COURT REDUCES CMB SHIPPING FINE.

text.p: The European Court of First Instance has reduced fines levied for anti-competitive behaviour against maritime transport companies operating between West Africa and Europe.
In a ruling on Tuesday, the court cut by 1 million European currency units ($1.2 million) fines on Compagnie Maritime Belge (CMB), Dafra Lines, Deutsche Afrika-Line and Nedlloyd Line Line.
All operate a shipping conference between ports in Zaire and the North Sea, with the exception of Britain.

In December 1992, the European Commission fined the four companies 10.1 million Ecus. The major part of the fine, 9.6 million Ecus, was levied against CMB, a group including Dafra and Deutsche Afrika-Lines.

Refusing to remove the fines outright, the court rejected a series of arguments put forth by the shippers that the Commission acted outside the law, that the shippers did not abuse a dominant position, that a shipping conference should be exempted from competition rules, and that the market concerned was outside of the Commission's jurisdiction.

The court explained that CMB took the largest fine because it played the leading role in the anti-competitive practices, a factor considered more relevant by the court than CMB's share in the conference earning's pool.
